column1: # K23 MRL-pruning differential cases, for probes/diff3.py.
# columns: pattern | outer_min | inner_min | stride | lengths | char | prefix | suffix
# The lengths are chosen around each shape's EXACT-MINIMUM boundary
# (n = outer_min * inner_min), which is where K23 lives, plus points above
# and below it. Every case must be python-`re`-feasible as well as
# pcrec-feasible, because python is the arm that says what the answer IS --
# so the family stops at (a{11,22}){11,50}, whose python arm already costs
# ~2.9 s; see k23_design.md section 3.3 for the growth curve that forces that
# ceiling.
# --- the K23 exemplar and its width siblings (the D27 characterization) ---
# --- the same shape reached by an UNANCHORED search that must skip bytes ---
# The clamp is stated against the SUBJECT END, not against the match start,
# so a match that begins late is the case that catches an off-by-a-prefix.
# --- a NON-EMPTY FOLLOW: the prototype passes follow-min 0, i.e. it
# UNDER-estimates minrest here. Under-estimating is the safe direction (it
# prunes less); these rows exist to show that the safe direction is the one
# the prototype actually takes, rather than to show a win.
# --- small nested shapes lifted from tests/base/d27_nesting.rxt ---
# --- nullable and unit-min inners: minrest collapses to 0 and the clamp
# must simply not be emitted (a clamp against n-0 is a no-op, but an
# off-by-one there would silently truncate every match)
# --- a NON-'a' body and a class body: the stride/derivation must not be
# reading the literal, and a nomatch subject must stay a nomatch
